$comment: ADR-0174 D11: the scenario registry the concurrency benchmark runs.
Each row pairs a G# scenario with the Go program's counterpart, so the
runner can report both a within-runtime regression check and a G#-vs-Go
ratio (informational, because it moves with the Go toolchain and the
A null `go` row means the scenario has NO Go counterpart, and several are
deliberately null (issue #3902 S1). A pairing is only honest when both
sides do the same work per counted operation: `rendezvous` counts one
hand-off where Go's pingpong counts two, `select-ready` performs four
channel operations where Go's select row performs one, and `chunks()`
copies elements where Go passes a slice header. Those rows are now G#-only,
the rows shaped to match Go's `[]int32` controls. The array rows remain G#-only
controls. Checksummed rows additionally require exact
counted-work parity across every measured runtime and launch.

scenarios.name: buf64
scenarios.what: A bounded channel driven producer-to-consumer: one pipeline stage.

scenarios.name: rendezvous
scenarios.what: Capacity 0, so the number is the hand-off rather than the buffer. ONE hand-off per operation; `pingpong` is the Go-paired counterpart.

scenarios.name: pingpong
scenarios.what: A round trip over two rendezvous channels: TWO hand-offs per counted operation, shaped exactly like Go's.

scenarios.name: closed-recv
scenarios.what: A receive from a closed, drained channel — the exception-based defect D2 removes.

scenarios.name: spawn
scenarios.what: Spawn cost: `go` is a thread-pool work item, not a Task. Times the spawn and the join only, as Go's WaitGroup row does.

scenarios.name: select-ready
scenarios.what: A select whose arms are ready: no registration, no park. Four channel operations per counted iteration, so G#-only; `select-stream` is the Go-paired row.

scenarios.name: select-stream
scenarios.what: One select receive per operation against a producer filling one buffered arm — a mix of ready and parked selects, as Go's row is.

scenarios.name: select-park
scenarios.what: A select with no ready arm: registration on every arm, a park, a hand-off. Wave 1 could not measure this at all.

scenarios.name: chunk64
scenarios.what: D10 batching at 64 elements per chunk. G#-only: `chunks()` copies elements where Go passes a slice header.

scenarios.name: chunk1k
scenarios.what: D10 batching at 1024 elements per chunk. The curve between this and chunk64 is the point, not either number.

scenarios.name: chunk64-arrays
scenarios.what: G#-only control: fresh CLR int32 arrays over capacity-64 channels at 64 elements.

scenarios.name: chunk1k-arrays
scenarios.what: G#-only control: fresh CLR int32 arrays over capacity-64 channels at 1024 elements with an exact-length tail.

scenarios.name: chunk64-slices
scenarios.what: Fresh native G# slices versus fresh Go []int32 slices over capacity-64 channels at 64 elements.

scenarios.name: chunk1k-slices
scenarios.what: Fresh native G# slices versus fresh Go []int32 slices over capacity-64 channels at 1024 elements with an exact-length tail.
